require "digest"
require "fileutils"
require "securerandom"
require "time"

module Syncbox
  module Server
    # Raised for a key that cannot name a blob on this server.
    class InvalidKeyError < StandardError; end

    # Blobs stored as regular files under <data_dir>/blobs/<key>. Uploads are
    # staged in <data_dir>/tmp and renamed into place, so a blob is never
    # visible half-written and staging files can never collide with a key.
    # rename(2) replaces the target atomically: a reader that opened the old
    # file keeps reading it, one that opens afterwards gets the new one, and of
    # concurrent puts to one key the last rename wins whole.
    class Store
      CHUNK_SIZE = 64 * 1024
      STAGING_SUFFIX = ".part"
      # Linux limits on a file name and a whole path (including its NUL).
      NAME_MAX = 255
      PATH_MAX = 4096
      # How many times put recreates parent directories removed under it.
      PUT_ATTEMPTS = 100

      # Errors from creating the blob's path that mean the key cannot be
      # represented here: a component is too long, or a file is in the way of
      # a directory (or the other way round).
      KEY_PATH_ERRORS = [
        Errno::ENAMETOOLONG, Errno::ENOTDIR, Errno::EISDIR, Errno::EEXIST,
        Errno::EILSEQ, Errno::EINVAL
      ].freeze

      # Checks a decoded key and returns it as a UTF-8 string. A key is a
      # relative POSIX path: no empty, "." or ".." segments, so it can't
      # escape the store or alias another key.
      def self.validate_key(key)
        key = key.b.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8)
        raise InvalidKeyError, "key is not valid UTF-8" unless key.valid_encoding?
        raise InvalidKeyError, "key contains a NUL byte" if key.include?("\0")

        segments = key.split("/", -1)
        if segments.empty? || segments.any? { |s| s.empty? || s == "." || s == ".." }
          raise InvalidKeyError, "key must be a relative path without empty, '.' or '..' segments"
        end

        key
      end

      def initialize(data_dir)
        # Paths are handled as raw bytes so that joining never hits an
        # encoding mismatch between the data dir and keys or file names.
        @blobs_dir = File.expand_path(File.join(data_dir, "blobs")).b
        @tmp_dir = File.join(data_dir, "tmp").b
      end

      # Readies the data dir before serving: creates the store's directories,
      # removes staging files left by a server killed mid-upload, and checks
      # that staged files can be renamed into the blobs dir. rename(2) fails
      # with EXDEV rather than copying when the two are on different
      # filesystems or mounts; this reports that up front instead of failing
      # every put. Assumes it is the only server using the data dir.
      def prepare!
        FileUtils.mkdir_p(@tmp_dir)
        FileUtils.mkdir_p(@blobs_dir)
        Dir.children(@tmp_dir, encoding: Encoding::BINARY).each do |name|
          FileUtils.rm_f(File.join(@tmp_dir, name)) if name.end_with?(STAGING_SUFFIX)
        end
        check_rename_into_store
      end

      # Stores the contents of io (nil means empty) under key, replacing any
      # existing blob. Returns {key:, sha256:, size:}.
      def put(key, io)
        key = self.class.validate_key(key)
        path = blob_path(key)
        # Checked up front: the kernel would only report this halfway through
        # creating the parent directories, leaving a partial chain behind.
        if path.bytesize >= PATH_MAX || key.split("/").any? { |s| s.bytesize > NAME_MAX }
          raise InvalidKeyError, "key is too long for the filesystem"
        end

        FileUtils.mkdir_p(@tmp_dir)
        FileUtils.mkdir_p(@blobs_dir)
        tmp = staging_path
        sha256, size = write_file(tmp, io)

        attempts = 0
        begin
          make_parent_dirs(key)
          raise InvalidKeyError, "key resolves outside the store" unless confined_on_disk?(path)

          File.rename(tmp, path)
        rescue Errno::ENOENT
          # A concurrent delete pruned a parent directory right after it was
          # created; create it again.
          retry if (attempts += 1) < PUT_ATTEMPTS
          raise
        rescue *KEY_PATH_ERRORS => e
          raise InvalidKeyError, "key cannot be stored as a file (#{e.class.name.split('::').last})"
        end

        { key: key, sha256: sha256, size: size }
      ensure
        FileUtils.rm_f(tmp) if tmp
      end

      # Opens the blob stored under key for reading, or returns nil if there
      # is none. The caller must close the returned File. The open handle
      # keeps serving the old contents if the blob is replaced meanwhile.
      def open(key)
        path = blob_path(self.class.validate_key(key))
        return nil unless confined_on_disk?(path)

        file = File.open(path, File::RDONLY | File::NOFOLLOW | File::BINARY)
        # Directories open fine on Linux; only regular files are blobs.
        return file if file.stat.file?

        file.close
        nil
      rescue Errno::ENOENT, Errno::ELOOP, *KEY_PATH_ERRORS
        nil
      end

      # Removes the blob stored under key; returns false if there is none.
      # As in the listing, only regular files reached through real directories
      # are blobs, so symlinks are neither followed nor removed. Directories
      # left empty are pruned so their paths can be used as keys again.
      def delete(key)
        path = blob_path(self.class.validate_key(key))
        return false unless blob_file?(path)

        begin
          File.unlink(path)
        rescue Errno::ENOENT
          return false # deleted concurrently
        end
        prune_empty_dirs(File.dirname(path))
        true
      end

      # Metadata of every blob, sorted by key. Entries that are not regular
      # files, have names that aren't valid UTF-8, or vanish or become
      # unreadable while listing are skipped rather than failing the listing.
      def list
        entries = []
        # Iterative walk: keys may nest thousands of directories deep, more
        # than a request thread's stack would allow with recursion.
        pending = [[@blobs_dir, nil]]
        until pending.empty?
          dir, prefix = pending.pop
          each_entry(dir, prefix) do |path, key, stat|
            if stat.directory?
              pending << [path, key]
            elsif stat.file?
              entries << blob_meta(path, key)
            end
          end
        end
        entries.compact.sort_by { |e| e[:key] }
      end

      private

      def staging_path
        File.join(@tmp_dir, "#{SecureRandom.hex(16)}#{STAGING_SUFFIX}")
      end

      # Renames a staged file into the blobs dir and removes it again. The
      # probe's name is not valid UTF-8, so even if the process dies before
      # removing it, it is never listed and no key can name it.
      def check_rename_into_store
        tmp = staging_path
        File.open(tmp, File::WRONLY | File::CREAT | File::EXCL, 0o600, &:close)
        probe = File.join(@blobs_dir, ".rename-probe-#{SecureRandom.hex(8)}-\xFF".b)
        File.rename(tmp, probe)
      ensure
        FileUtils.rm_f(tmp) if tmp
        FileUtils.rm_f(probe) if probe
      end

      # The on-disk path of a validated key. Besides the segment checks in
      # validate_key, the normalized path must lie strictly inside the blobs
      # dir, so no spelling of a key can name the dir itself or leave it.
      def blob_path(key)
        # Joined first: expand_path must never get the key as its own argument,
        # where a leading "~" would be expanded to a home directory.
        path = File.expand_path(File.join(@blobs_dir, key.b)).b
        raise InvalidKeyError, "key resolves outside the store" unless path.start_with?("#{@blobs_dir}/")

        path
      end

      # Whether path stays inside the blobs dir once symlinks are resolved:
      # the deepest existing directory above it must resolve to itself, i.e.
      # no symlink (not even one pointing back inside) sits between the blobs
      # dir and the blob. Parts that don't exist yet can't redirect anywhere.
      def confined_on_disk?(path)
        dir = File.dirname(path)
        loop do
          dir = File.dirname(dir) until dir == @blobs_dir || entry_exists?(dir)
          begin
            return File.realpath(dir).b == File.realpath(@blobs_dir).b + dir.byteslice(@blobs_dir.bytesize..)
          rescue Errno::ENOENT
            return false if dir == @blobs_dir

            # A concurrent delete pruned the directory meanwhile; look further up.
          end
        end
      rescue SystemCallError
        false
      end

      # Like File.exist?, but true for a symlink whatever it points at.
      def entry_exists?(path)
        File.lstat(path)
        true
      rescue Errno::ENOENT
        false
      end

      def write_file(path, io)
        digest = Digest::SHA256.new
        size = 0
        File.open(path, File::WRONLY | File::CREAT | File::EXCL | File::BINARY, 0o644) do |f|
          buf = String.new(capacity: CHUNK_SIZE)
          while io&.read(CHUNK_SIZE, buf)
            digest << buf
            size += buf.bytesize
            f.write(buf)
          end
          f.flush
          f.fsync
        end
        [digest.hexdigest, size]
      end

      # Creates the directories above key's blob. Unlike FileUtils.mkdir_p this
      # tells a non-directory in the way (EEXIST: the key can't be stored)
      # from a directory that another put created and a concurrent delete
      # pruned right away (ENOENT: put retries).
      def make_parent_dirs(key)
        dir = @blobs_dir
        key.b.split("/")[0...-1].each do |segment|
          dir = File.join(dir, segment)
          begin
            Dir.mkdir(dir)
          rescue Errno::EEXIST
            # lstat raises ENOENT if the entry is gone again; if it was
            # recreated meanwhile it is a directory and all is well. A symlink
            # is never descended into, even if it points at a directory.
            raise unless File.lstat(dir).directory?
          end
        end
      end

      # Whether path is a regular file (not a symlink to one) reached without
      # passing through a symlink.
      def blob_file?(path)
        confined_on_disk?(path) && File.lstat(path).file?
      rescue Errno::ENOENT, Errno::ELOOP, *KEY_PATH_ERRORS
        false
      end

      # Removes dir and its parents up to (not including) the blobs dir for as
      # long as they are empty.
      def prune_empty_dirs(dir)
        while dir.bytesize > @blobs_dir.bytesize
          Dir.rmdir(dir)
          dir = File.dirname(dir)
        end
      rescue SystemCallError
        # Not empty (or already gone): the remaining parents are in use.
      end

      # Yields path, key and lstat of each entry of dir with a UTF-8 name.
      def each_entry(dir, prefix)
        Dir.children(dir, encoding: Encoding::BINARY).each do |raw_name|
          name = raw_name.dup.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8)
          next unless name.valid_encoding?

          path = File.join(dir, raw_name)
          begin
            stat = File.lstat(path)
          rescue SystemCallError
            next
          end
          yield path, prefix ? "#{prefix}/#{name}" : name, stat
        end
      rescue SystemCallError
        # Directory missing (nothing stored yet), replaced or unreadable.
      end

      # Size, mtime and hash all come from one open handle, so they describe
      # the same version even if the blob is replaced while it is being read.
      def blob_meta(path, key)
        File.open(path, File::RDONLY | File::NOFOLLOW | File::BINARY) do |f|
          stat = f.stat
          return nil unless stat.file?

          digest = Digest::SHA256.new
          buf = String.new(capacity: CHUNK_SIZE)
          digest << buf while f.read(CHUNK_SIZE, buf)
          { key: key, size: stat.size, sha256: digest.hexdigest, modified_at: stat.mtime.utc.iso8601(6) }
        end
      rescue SystemCallError
        nil
      end
    end
  end
end

require "json"
require "uri"

module Syncbox
  module Server
    # Rack application implementing the Syncbox HTTP API.
    class App
      BLOB_PREFIX = "/blobs/"

      # Response body streaming an open file in chunks; closes it when done.
      class FileBody
        def initialize(file)
          @file = file
        end

        def each
          while (chunk = @file.read(Store::CHUNK_SIZE))
            yield chunk
          end
        end

        def close
          @file.close
        end
      end

      def initialize(config)
        @config = config
        @store = Store.new(config.data_dir)
      end

      def call(env)
        # Request paths are raw bytes and may be anything a client sent.
        path = env["PATH_INFO"].to_s.b
        method = env["REQUEST_METHOD"]

        if path == "/healthz"
          return method_not_allowed("GET, HEAD") unless %w[GET HEAD].include?(method)

          text(200, "ok\n")
        elsif path == "/blobs"
          return method_not_allowed("GET, HEAD") unless %w[GET HEAD].include?(method)

          json(200, @store.list)
        elsif path.start_with?(BLOB_PREFIX) && method == "PUT"
          put_blob(path.delete_prefix(BLOB_PREFIX), env["rack.input"])
        elsif path.start_with?(BLOB_PREFIX) && %w[GET HEAD].include?(method)
          get_blob(path.delete_prefix(BLOB_PREFIX))
        elsif path.start_with?(BLOB_PREFIX) && method == "DELETE"
          delete_blob(path.delete_prefix(BLOB_PREFIX))
        else
          text(404, "not found\n")
        end
      end

      private

      def put_blob(raw_key, input)
        json(201, @store.put(decode_key(raw_key), input))
      rescue InvalidKeyError => e
        text(400, "invalid key: #{e.message}\n")
      end

      def get_blob(raw_key)
        file = @store.open(decode_key(raw_key))
        return text(404, "not found\n") unless file

        headers = { "content-type" => "application/octet-stream", "content-length" => file.size.to_s }
        [200, headers, FileBody.new(file)]
      rescue InvalidKeyError => e
        text(400, "invalid key: #{e.message}\n")
      end

      def delete_blob(raw_key)
        return text(404, "not found\n") unless @store.delete(decode_key(raw_key))

        [204, {}, []]
      rescue InvalidKeyError => e
        text(400, "invalid key: #{e.message}\n")
      end

      # Percent-decodes the key part of the path ("+" stays literal).
      def decode_key(raw_key)
        URI.decode_uri_component(raw_key, Encoding::BINARY)
      rescue ArgumentError
        raise InvalidKeyError, "malformed percent-encoding"
      end

      def text(status, body, headers = {})
        [status, { "content-type" => "text/plain; charset=utf-8" }.merge(headers), [body]]
      end

      def json(status, data)
        [status, { "content-type" => "application/json" }, [JSON.generate(data)]]
      end

      def method_not_allowed(allow)
        text(405, "method not allowed\n", "allow" => allow)
      end
    end
  end
end

require "digest"
require "fileutils"
require "securerandom"
require "time"

module Syncbox
  module Server
    # Raised for a key that cannot name a blob on this server.
    class InvalidKeyError < StandardError; end

    # Blobs stored as regular files under <data_dir>/blobs/<key>. Uploads are
    # staged in <data_dir>/tmp and renamed into place, so a blob is never
    # visible half-written and staging files can never collide with a key.
    # rename(2) replaces the target atomically: a reader that opened the old
    # file keeps reading it, one that opens afterwards gets the new one, and of
    # concurrent puts to one key the last rename wins whole.
    class Store
      CHUNK_SIZE = 64 * 1024
      STAGING_SUFFIX = ".part"
      # Linux limits on a file name and a whole path (including its NUL).
      NAME_MAX = 255
      PATH_MAX = 4096
      # How many times put recreates parent directories removed under it.
      PUT_ATTEMPTS = 100

      # Errors from creating the blob's path that mean the key cannot be
      # represented here: a component is too long, or a file is in the way of
      # a directory (or the other way round).
      KEY_PATH_ERRORS = [
        Errno::ENAMETOOLONG, Errno::ENOTDIR, Errno::EISDIR, Errno::EEXIST,
        Errno::EILSEQ, Errno::EINVAL
      ].freeze

      # Checks a decoded key and returns it as a UTF-8 string. A key is a
      # relative POSIX path: no empty, "." or ".." segments, so it can't
      # escape the store or alias another key.
      def self.validate_key(key)
        key = key.b.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8)
        raise InvalidKeyError, "key is not valid UTF-8" unless key.valid_encoding?
        raise InvalidKeyError, "key contains a NUL byte" if key.include?("\0")

        segments = key.split("/", -1)
        if segments.empty? || segments.any? { |s| s.empty? || s == "." || s == ".." }
          raise InvalidKeyError, "key must be a relative path without empty, '.' or '..' segments"
        end

        key
      end

      def initialize(data_dir)
        # Paths are handled as raw bytes so that joining never hits an
        # encoding mismatch between the data dir and keys or file names.
        @blobs_dir = File.expand_path(File.join(data_dir, "blobs")).b
        @tmp_dir = File.join(data_dir, "tmp").b
      end

      # Readies the data dir before serving: creates the store's directories,
      # removes staging files left by a server killed mid-upload, and checks
      # that staged files can be renamed into the blobs dir. rename(2) fails
      # with EXDEV rather than copying when the two are on different
      # filesystems or mounts; this reports that up front instead of failing
      # every put. Assumes it is the only server using the data dir.
      def prepare!
        FileUtils.mkdir_p(@tmp_dir)
        FileUtils.mkdir_p(@blobs_dir)
        Dir.children(@tmp_dir, encoding: Encoding::BINARY).each do |name|
          FileUtils.rm_f(File.join(@tmp_dir, name)) if name.end_with?(STAGING_SUFFIX)
        end
        check_rename_into_store
      end

      # Stores the contents of io (nil means empty) under key, replacing any
      # existing blob. Returns {key:, sha256:, size:}.
      def put(key, io)
        key = self.class.validate_key(key)
        path = blob_path(key)
        # Checked up front: the kernel would only report this halfway through
        # creating the parent directories, leaving a partial chain behind.
        if path.bytesize >= PATH_MAX || key.split("/").any? { |s| s.bytesize > NAME_MAX }
          raise InvalidKeyError, "key is too long for the filesystem"
        end

        FileUtils.mkdir_p(@tmp_dir)
        FileUtils.mkdir_p(@blobs_dir)
        tmp = staging_path
        sha256, size = write_file(tmp, io)

        attempts = 0
        begin
          make_parent_dirs(key)
          raise InvalidKeyError, "key resolves outside the store" unless confined_on_disk?(path)

          File.rename(tmp, path)
        rescue Errno::ENOENT
          # A concurrent delete pruned a parent directory right after it was
          # created; create it again.
          retry if (attempts += 1) < PUT_ATTEMPTS
          raise
        rescue *KEY_PATH_ERRORS => e
          raise InvalidKeyError, "key cannot be stored as a file (#{e.class.name.split('::').last})"
        end

        { key: key, sha256: sha256, size: size }
      ensure
        FileUtils.rm_f(tmp) if tmp
      end

      # Opens the blob stored under key for reading, or returns nil if there
      # is none. The caller must close the returned File. The open handle
      # keeps serving the old contents if the blob is replaced meanwhile.
      def open(key)
        path = blob_path(self.class.validate_key(key))
        return nil unless confined_on_disk?(path)

        file = File.open(path, File::RDONLY | File::NOFOLLOW | File::BINARY)
        # Directories open fine on Linux; only regular files are blobs.
        return file if file.stat.file?

        file.close
        nil
      rescue Errno::ENOENT, Errno::ELOOP, *KEY_PATH_ERRORS
        nil
      end

      # Removes the blob stored under key; returns false if there is none.
      # As in the listing, only regular files reached through real directories
      # are blobs, so symlinks are neither followed nor removed. Directories
      # left empty are pruned so their paths can be used as keys again.
      def delete(key)
        path = blob_path(self.class.validate_key(key))
        return false unless blob_file?(path)

        begin
          File.unlink(path)
        rescue Errno::ENOENT
          return false # deleted concurrently
        end
        prune_empty_dirs(File.dirname(path))
        true
      end

      # Metadata of every blob, sorted by key. Entries that are not regular
      # files, have names that aren't valid UTF-8, or vanish or become
      # unreadable while listing are skipped rather than failing the listing.
      def list
        entries = []
        # Iterative walk: keys may nest thousands of directories deep, more
        # than a request thread's stack would allow with recursion.
        pending = [[@blobs_dir, nil]]
        until pending.empty?
          dir, prefix = pending.pop
          each_entry(dir, prefix) do |path, key, stat|
            if stat.directory?
              pending << [path, key]
            elsif stat.file?
              entries << blob_meta(path, key)
            end
          end
        end
        entries.compact.sort_by { |e| e[:key] }
      end

      private

      def staging_path
        File.join(@tmp_dir, "#{SecureRandom.hex(16)}#{STAGING_SUFFIX}")
      end

      # Renames a staged file into the blobs dir and removes it again. The
      # probe's name is not valid UTF-8, so even if the process dies before
      # removing it, it is never listed and no key can name it.
      def check_rename_into_store
        tmp = staging_path
        File.open(tmp, File::WRONLY | File::CREAT | File::EXCL, 0o600, &:close)
        probe = File.join(@blobs_dir, ".rename-probe-#{SecureRandom.hex(8)}-\xFF".b)
        File.rename(tmp, probe)
      ensure
        FileUtils.rm_f(tmp) if tmp
        FileUtils.rm_f(probe) if probe
      end

      # The on-disk path of a validated key. Besides the segment checks in
      # validate_key, the normalized path must lie strictly inside the blobs
      # dir, so no spelling of a key can name the dir itself or leave it.
      def blob_path(key)
        # Joined first: expand_path must never get the key as its own argument,
        # where a leading "~" would be expanded to a home directory.
        path = File.expand_path(File.join(@blobs_dir, key.b)).b
        raise InvalidKeyError, "key resolves outside the store" unless path.start_with?("#{@blobs_dir}/")

        path
      end

      # Whether path stays inside the blobs dir once symlinks are resolved:
      # the deepest existing directory above it must resolve to itself, i.e.
      # no symlink (not even one pointing back inside) sits between the blobs
      # dir and the blob. Parts that don't exist yet can't redirect anywhere.
      def confined_on_disk?(path)
        dir = File.dirname(path)
        loop do
          dir = File.dirname(dir) until dir == @blobs_dir || entry_exists?(dir)
          begin
            return File.realpath(dir).b == File.realpath(@blobs_dir).b + dir.byteslice(@blobs_dir.bytesize..)
          rescue Errno::ENOENT
            return false if dir == @blobs_dir

            # A concurrent delete pruned the directory meanwhile; look further up.
          end
        end
      rescue SystemCallError
        false
      end

      # Like File.exist?, but true for a symlink whatever it points at.
      def entry_exists?(path)
        File.lstat(path)
        true
      rescue Errno::ENOENT
        false
      end

      def write_file(path, io)
        digest = Digest::SHA256.new
        size = 0
        File.open(path, File::WRONLY | File::CREAT | File::EXCL | File::BINARY, 0o644) do |f|
          buf = String.new(capacity: CHUNK_SIZE)
          while io&.read(CHUNK_SIZE, buf)
            digest << buf
            size += buf.bytesize
            f.write(buf)
          end
          f.flush
          f.fsync
        end
        [digest.hexdigest, size]
      end

      # Creates the directories above key's blob. Unlike FileUtils.mkdir_p this
      # tells a non-directory in the way (EEXIST: the key can't be stored)
      # from a directory that another put created and a concurrent delete
      # pruned right away (ENOENT: put retries).
      def make_parent_dirs(key)
        dir = @blobs_dir
        key.b.split("/")[0...-1].each do |segment|
          dir = File.join(dir, segment)
          begin
            Dir.mkdir(dir)
          rescue Errno::EEXIST
            # lstat raises ENOENT if the entry is gone again; if it was
            # recreated meanwhile it is a directory and all is well. A symlink
            # is never descended into, even if it points at a directory.
            raise unless File.lstat(dir).directory?
          end
        end
      end

      # Whether path is a regular file (not a symlink to one) reached without
      # passing through a symlink.
      def blob_file?(path)
        confined_on_disk?(path) && File.lstat(path).file?
      rescue Errno::ENOENT, Errno::ELOOP, *KEY_PATH_ERRORS
        false
      end

      # Removes dir and its parents up to (not including) the blobs dir for as
      # long as they are empty.
      def prune_empty_dirs(dir)
        while dir.bytesize > @blobs_dir.bytesize
          Dir.rmdir(dir)
          dir = File.dirname(dir)
        end
      rescue SystemCallError
        # Not empty (or already gone): the remaining parents are in use.
      end

      # Yields path, key and lstat of each entry of dir with a UTF-8 name.
      def each_entry(dir, prefix)
        Dir.children(dir, encoding: Encoding::BINARY).each do |raw_name|
          name = raw_name.dup.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8)
          next unless name.valid_encoding?

          path = File.join(dir, raw_name)
          begin
            stat = File.lstat(path)
          rescue SystemCallError
            next
          end
          yield path, prefix ? "#{prefix}/#{name}" : name, stat
        end
      rescue SystemCallError
        # Directory missing (nothing stored yet), replaced or unreadable.
      end

      # Size, mtime and hash all come from one open handle, so they describe
      # the same version even if the blob is replaced while it is being read.
      def blob_meta(path, key)
        File.open(path, File::RDONLY | File::NOFOLLOW | File::BINARY) do |f|
          stat = f.stat
          return nil unless stat.file?

          digest = Digest::SHA256.new
          buf = String.new(capacity: CHUNK_SIZE)
          digest << buf while f.read(CHUNK_SIZE, buf)
          { key: key, size: stat.size, sha256: digest.hexdigest, modified_at: stat.mtime.utc.iso8601(6) }
        end
      rescue SystemCallError
        nil
      end
    end
  end
end

require "json"
require "uri"

module Syncbox
  module Server
    # Rack application implementing the Syncbox HTTP API.
    class App
      BLOB_PREFIX = "/blobs/"

      # Response body streaming an open file in chunks; closes it when done.
      class FileBody
        def initialize(file)
          @file = file
        end

        def each
          while (chunk = @file.read(Store::CHUNK_SIZE))
            yield chunk
          end
        end

        def close
          @file.close
        end
      end

      def initialize(config)
        @config = config
        @store = Store.new(config.data_dir)
      end

      def call(env)
        # Request paths are raw bytes and may be anything a client sent.
        path = env["PATH_INFO"].to_s.b
        method = env["REQUEST_METHOD"]

        if path == "/healthz"
          return method_not_allowed("GET, HEAD") unless %w[GET HEAD].include?(method)

          text(200, "ok\n")
        elsif path == "/blobs"
          return method_not_allowed("GET, HEAD") unless %w[GET HEAD].include?(method)

          json(200, @store.list)
        elsif path.start_with?(BLOB_PREFIX) && method == "PUT"
          put_blob(path.delete_prefix(BLOB_PREFIX), env["rack.input"])
        elsif path.start_with?(BLOB_PREFIX) && %w[GET HEAD].include?(method)
          get_blob(path.delete_prefix(BLOB_PREFIX))
        elsif path.start_with?(BLOB_PREFIX) && method == "DELETE"
          delete_blob(path.delete_prefix(BLOB_PREFIX))
        else
          text(404, "not found\n")
        end
      end

      private

      def put_blob(raw_key, input)
        json(201, @store.put(decode_key(raw_key), input))
      rescue InvalidKeyError => e
        text(400, "invalid key: #{e.message}\n")
      end

      def get_blob(raw_key)
        file = @store.open(decode_key(raw_key))
        return text(404, "not found\n") unless file

        headers = { "content-type" => "application/octet-stream", "content-length" => file.size.to_s }
        [200, headers, FileBody.new(file)]
      rescue InvalidKeyError => e
        text(400, "invalid key: #{e.message}\n")
      end

      def delete_blob(raw_key)
        return text(404, "not found\n") unless @store.delete(decode_key(raw_key))

        [204, {}, []]
      rescue InvalidKeyError => e
        text(400, "invalid key: #{e.message}\n")
      end

      # Percent-decodes the key part of the path ("+" stays literal).
      def decode_key(raw_key)
        URI.decode_uri_component(raw_key, Encoding::BINARY)
      rescue ArgumentError
        raise InvalidKeyError, "malformed percent-encoding"
      end

      def text(status, body, headers = {})
        [status, { "content-type" => "text/plain; charset=utf-8" }.merge(headers), [body]]
      end

      def json(status, data)
        [status, { "content-type" => "application/json" }, [JSON.generate(data)]]
      end

      def method_not_allowed(allow)
        text(405, "method not allowed\n", "allow" => allow)
      end
    end
  end
end

1	# Syncbox (Ruby)
2	
3	Self-hosted file storage with sync: HTTP server + CLI client.
4	Contract: [SYNCBOX-SPEC.md](SYNCBOX-SPEC.md), [syncbox-openapi.yaml](syncbox-openapi.yaml).
5	
6	Everything runs in Docker via `docker compose` (Ruby 3.3.12, `ruby:3.3.12` image);
7	nothing needs to be installed on the host besides Docker.
8	
9	## Server
10	
11	```sh
12	./run-server --data-dir <path> [--port <n>]   # port defaults to 8080
13	SYNCBOX_DATA_DIR=<path> SYNCBOX_PORT=<n> ./run-server
14	```
15	
16	Flags take precedence over environment variables. The data dir is created if
17	missing and bind-mounted into the container; the port is published on
18	`127.0.0.1` (override with `SYNCBOX_PUBLISH_ADDR=0.0.0.0`). The server runs in
19	the foreground; SIGTERM/SIGINT stop it gracefully and remove the container.
20	
21	Implemented endpoints: `GET /healthz`, `GET /blobs`, `PUT /blobs/{key}`, `GET /blobs/{key}`,
22	`DELETE /blobs/{key}`. Blobs are stored under `<data-dir>/blobs/<key>`; uploads
23	are staged in `<data-dir>/tmp`.
24	
25	### Atomic uploads
26	
27	`PUT` streams the body into a fresh staging file `<data-dir>/tmp/<random>.part`
28	(fsynced), then `rename(2)`s it over `<data-dir>/blobs/<key>`. Consequences:
29	
30	- A `GET` or `GET /blobs` sees either the whole old blob or the whole new one,
31	  never a partial write; a download already in progress keeps streaming the
32	  version it opened.
33	- Concurrent `PUT`s to the same key each report the hash of their own body; the
34	  last rename wins and the stored blob is one of the uploaded bodies, intact.
35	  `PUT`s to different keys share nothing but the directories above them.
36	- Parent directories of a new key are created only after the whole body is staged.
37	- Staging files are outside `blobs/`, so they're never listed or reachable by
38	  any key, and they are removed when the request ends, whether it succeeded or
39	  failed. A body cut short by the client never reaches the app (Puma buffers
40	  the body first). Files left by a server killed mid-upload are removed on the
41	  next start.
42	- On startup the server checks that a file can be renamed from `tmp/` into
43	  `blobs/`, and refuses to start if not (e.g. `blobs/` is a separate
44	  filesystem or mount): `rename(2)` is atomic only within one mount and fails
45	  with `EXDEV` across mounts — it never falls back to copying.
46	
47	Coordination between several server processes on one data dir is out of scope.
48	
49	`GET /blobs` returns `[{"key", "size", "sha256", "modified_at"}]` for every
50	regular file under `<data-dir>/blobs`, sorted by key (`modified_at` is the file
51	mtime, ISO 8601 UTC). Files placed there directly are listed too; symlinks,
52	special files and names that aren't valid UTF-8 are skipped. Hashes are
53	computed on each request.
54	
55	`DELETE /blobs/{key}` answers `204` (no body) when the blob was removed and `404`
56	when there is none — directories and symlinks are not blobs, so they are never
57	followed or removed. Directories left empty by a delete are pruned, so their
58	paths can become keys again.
59	
60	### Keys and directory traversal
61	
62	A key is a relative POSIX path (`docs/readme.txt`). `PUT`, `GET` and `DELETE
63	/blobs/{key}` answer `400` for a key that:
64	
65	- contains a `..` segment, or a `.`/empty segment (`a//b`, `a/`), or is absolute
66	  (`/etc/passwd`, `%2Fetc%2Fpasswd`) — `%2F` counts as a separator, `%2e` as a dot;
67	- can't be a file name here: not valid UTF-8 after percent-decoding (incl.
68	  encoded surrogates and overlong forms such as `%C0%AE`), contains NUL, has
69	  malformed percent-escapes, or exceeds `NAME_MAX`/`PATH_MAX`.
70	
71	`..` inside a name (`a..b`, `...`) is an ordinary character sequence. On top
72	of these textual checks the store confines the actual disk path: the
73	normalized path must lie strictly inside `<data-dir>/blobs`, and resolving it
74	with `realpath` must not change it, so a symlink placed in the store by hand is
75	never followed (`PUT` through it is `400`, `GET`/`DELETE` are `404`). The data
76	dir itself may be a symlink.
77	
78	## Client
79	
80	```sh
81	./run-client push <dir> --server <url>
82	./run-client pull <dir> --server <url>
83	./run-client status <dir> --server <url>
84	SYNCBOX_SERVER=<url> ./run-client push <dir>
85	```
86	
87	`--server` takes precedence over `SYNCBOX_SERVER`; it must be an `http://` or
88	`https://` URL (a path prefix such as `http://host/syncbox` is allowed). The
89	client runs in the `client` compose service: `<dir>` must be an existing
90	directory and is bind-mounted into the container (read-only for `status`),
91	which uses the host's network, so `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` reaches a server
92	started with `run-server` on this machine. SIGTERM/SIGINT stop the container.
93	
94	`push` walks `<dir>` recursively, hashes every regular file with SHA-256 and
95	compares it with `GET /blobs`. It `PUT`s the files that the server lacks or holds
96	with a different hash, under the file's relative POSIX path as the key
97	(`docs/readme.txt`). Files identical to the server's version are not sent again,
98	and blobs that exist only on the server are left alone. Each upload is printed
99	(`uploaded <key>`), then a summary (`push: N uploaded, M unchanged`).
100	Symlinks (never followed), special files and names that aren't valid UTF-8
101	are skipped with a warning on stderr.
102	
103	`pull` is the reverse: it fetches `GET /blobs`, and `GET`s every blob that is
104	missing in `<dir>` or whose local file has a different SHA-256, writing it to
105	the key's relative POSIX path and creating directories as needed. Files
106	identical to the server's version are not downloaded again, and local files
107	the server doesn't have are left alone. Each download is printed
108	(`downloaded <key>`), then a summary (`pull: N downloaded, M unchanged`).
109	A download is streamed into a staging file next to its target
110	(`.syncbox-<random>.part`, removed on failure) and renamed over it once
111	complete, so a failed or interrupted pull never leaves a half-written file; a
112	body cut short of its `Content-Length` counts as a failure. A replaced file
113	keeps its permissions. Keys come from the server, so pull never writes
114	outside `<dir>`: keys that aren't plain relative paths (`..`, absolute, empty
115	or `.` segments, NUL) are skipped with a warning, and so are keys whose path
116	runs through a symlink (never followed) or ends at a symlink or special file
117	(never replaced).
118	
119	`status` is a dry run of `push` and `pull`: it compares `<dir>` with
120	`GET /blobs` by key and SHA-256, by the same rules, and prints what they would
121	do, changing nothing on either side. Its only request is `GET /blobs` (no
122	`PUT`/`DELETE`, not even a blob download), local files are only read, and
123	`run-client` mounts `<dir>` read-only for it. Each difference is one line,
124	uploads first, then downloads, each sorted by key:
125	
126	```
127	upload    new      local-only.txt      # push would upload it; the server lacks it
128	upload    changed  both.txt            # push would upload it; the server's copy differs
129	download  changed  both.txt            # pull would download it; the local copy differs
130	download  new      docs/remote.txt     # pull would download it; it is missing locally
131	status: 2 to upload, 2 to download, 1 unchanged
132	```
133	
134	A file whose contents differ is listed in both directions, as `push` and `pull`
135	would each overwrite the other side's copy; which one wins is up to `sync`.
136	With no differences it prints `status: in sync, N unchanged`. It skips, with the
137	same warnings, whatever `push` and `pull` would skip; a key that `pull` couldn't
138	write because a file or directory is in the way is reported on stderr
139	(`syncbox: cannot download a/b: a is not a directory`) instead of failing.
140	Exit status is `0` whenever the comparison succeeds, whether or not anything
141	differs.
142	
143	Exit status: `0` on success, `2` for a bad command line, `1` if the command
144	fails (server unreachable, the server rejects a request, a local file can't be
145	read or written, a file is in the way of a directory or the other way round
146	during a pull): the client prints the reason to stderr and stops at the first
147	failure.
148	
149	`sync` accepts the same arguments but is not implemented yet: it prints a
150	message saying so and exits with `1`.
151

162	- `bin/syncbox-server` — server entry point (inside the container)
163	- `bin/syncbox` — client CLI entry point (inside the container)
164	- `lib/syncbox/server/config.rb` — flag/env configuration
165	- `lib/syncbox/server/app.rb` — Rack app (HTTP API)

222	#!/usr/bin/env bash
223	# Runs the Syncbox client inside Docker (via docker compose).
224	#
225	#   run-client <push|pull|sync|status> <dir> --server <url>
226	#
227	# --server falls back to SYNCBOX_SERVER. <dir> is bind-mounted into the
228	# container; the container uses the host's network, so the server URL means
229	# the same as it does here (read-only for status). Exits with the client's
230	# status.
231	set -euo pipefail
232	
233	root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
234	
235	usage() {
236	  echo "Usage: run-client <push|pull|sync|status> <dir> --server <url>" >&2
237	  exit 2
238	}
239	
240	die() {
241	  echo "run-client: $*" >&2
242	  usage
243	}
244	
245	server="${SYNCBOX_SERVER:-}"
246	positional=()
247	
248	while (($#)); do
249	  case "$1" in
250	    --server) (($# >= 2)) || die "--server requires a value"; server="$2"; shift 2 ;;
251	    --server=*) server="${1#*=}"; shift ;;
252	    -h | --help) usage ;;
253	    --) shift; positional+=("$@"); break ;;
254	    -*) die "unknown option: $1" ;;
255	    *) positional+=("$1"); shift ;;
256	  esac
257	done
258	
259	((${#positional[@]} >= 1)) || die "missing command"
260	command="${positional[0]}"
261	case "$command" in
262	  push | pull | sync | status) ;;
263	  *) die "unknown command: $command" ;;
264	esac
265	((${#positional[@]} >= 2)) || die "missing <dir>"
266	((${#positional[@]} == 2)) || die "unexpected argument: ${positional[2]}"
267	dir="${positional[1]}"
268	[[ -n "$dir" ]] || die "missing <dir>"
269	[[ -n "$server" ]] || die "--server (or SYNCBOX_SERVER) is required"
270	
271	if [[ ! -e "$dir" ]]; then
272	  echo "run-client: $dir: no such directory" >&2
273	  exit 1
274	elif [[ ! -d "$dir" ]]; then
275	  echo "run-client: $dir: not a directory" >&2
276	  exit 1
277	fi
278	
279	export SYNCBOX_HOST_SYNC_DIR="$(cd -- "$dir" && pwd -P)"
280	export SYNCBOX_UID="$(id -u)" SYNCBOX_GID="$(id -g)"
281	# status is a dry run: give it the directory read-only.
282	if [[ "$command" == status ]]; then
283	  export SYNCBOX_SYNC_READ_ONLY=true
284	else
285	  export SYNCBOX_SYNC_READ_ONLY=false
286	fi
287	
288	compose=(docker compose --project-directory "$root" -f "$root/compose.yaml")
289	
290	# `docker compose run` does not forward SIGTERM to the container and leaves it
291	# running when killed, so stop our container explicitly on shutdown signals.
292	container="syncbox-client-$$"
293	child=""
294	stopping=""
295	
296	stop_container() {
297	  # Retry briefly in case the signal arrived before the container was created.
298	  for _ in $(seq 50); do
299	    docker stop --time 10 "$container" >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
300	    kill -0 "$child" 2>/dev/null || return 0
301	    sleep 0.2
302	  done
303	}
304	
305	on_signal() {
306	  trap '' TERM INT HUP
307	  stopping=1
308	  if [[ -n "$child" ]]; then stop_container; fi
309	  return 0
310	}
311	
312	trap on_signal TERM INT HUP
313	
314	"${compose[@]}" build --quiet client >&2
315	[[ -z "$stopping" ]] || exit 130
316	
317	# -T: no pseudo-TTY, so the client's stdout and stderr stay separate streams.
318	"${compose[@]}" run --rm -T --name "$container" client "$command" /sync --server "$server" &
319	child=$!
320	if [[ -n "$stopping" ]]; then stop_container; fi
321	
322	while kill -0 "$child" 2>/dev/null; do
323	  wait "$child" || true
324	done
325	status=0
326	wait "$child" || status=$?
327	[[ -z "$stopping" ]] || exit 130
328	exit "$status"

459	module Syncbox
460	  module Client
461	    # The files of a local directory tree, named by blob key: the file's
462	    # relative POSIX path inside the directory (docs/readme.txt).
463	    class LocalDir
464	      Entry = Data.define(:key, :path)
465	      # Where a key's file goes: stat is the File::Stat of the regular file
466	      # already there, or nil if there is none yet.
467	      Target = Data.define(:key, :path, :stat)
468	
469	      # A file is in the way of one of a key's directories, or a directory
470	      # is where its file would go.
471	      class PathConflict < Error
472	        attr_reader :key, :reason
473	
474	        def initialize(key, reason)
475	          super("cannot write #{key}: #{reason}")
476	          @key = key
477	          @reason = reason
478	        end
479	      end
480	
481	      # Downloads are staged next to their file under such names.
482	      STAGING_PREFIX = ".syncbox-"
483	      STAGING_SUFFIX = ".part"
484	
485	      # Whether key names a path inside the directory: a relative POSIX path
486	      # of valid UTF-8 without NUL and without empty, "." or ".." segments,
487	      # the same rule the server applies.
488	      def self.valid_key?(key)
489	        key.is_a?(String) && !key.empty? && key.encoding == Encoding::UTF_8 && key.valid_encoding? &&
490	          !key.include?("\0") && key.split("/", -1).none? { |s| s.empty? || s == "." || s == ".." }
491	      end
492	
493	      # An error's description without the (container-side) path it names.
494	      def self.reason(error)
495	        error.is_a?(SystemCallError) ? SystemCallError.new(nil, error.errno).message : error.message
496	      end
497	
498	      # SHA-256 (hex) of an entry's contents.
499	      def self.sha256(entry)
500	        Digest::SHA256.file(entry.path).hexdigest
501	      rescue SystemCallError, IOError => e
502	        raise Error, "cannot read #{entry.key}: #{reason(e)}"
503	      end
504	
505	      # on_skip is called with (relative path, reason) for each entry that
506	      # can't be synced: symlinks, special files, names that aren't UTF-8.
507	      def initialize(root, on_skip: nil)
508	        @root = root
509	        @on_skip = on_skip || ->(_path, _reason) {}
510	      end
511	
512	      # Every regular file under root, sorted by key. Symlinks are not
513	      # followed, just like the server never follows them in its store.
514	      def entries
515	        raise Error, "#{@root}: no such directory" unless File.exist?(@root)
516	        raise Error, "#{@root}: not a directory" unless File.directory?(@root)
517	
518	        found = []
519	        # Iterative walk, so deep trees can't exhaust the stack.
520	        pending = [[@root.b, nil]]
521	        until pending.empty?
522	          dir, prefix = pending.pop
523	          children(dir, prefix).each do |raw_name|
524	            path = File.join(dir, raw_name)
525	            rel = prefix ? "#{prefix}/#{raw_name}".b : raw_name
526	            stat = lstat(path, rel)
527	            next unless stat
528	
529	            key = rel.dup.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8)
530	            if !key.valid_encoding?
531	              @on_skip.call(key.scrub, "name is not valid UTF-8")
532	            elsif stat.directory?
533	              pending << [path, rel]
534	            elsif stat.file?
535	              found << Entry.new(key: key, path: path)
536	            elsif stat.symlink?
537	              @on_skip.call(key, "symbolic link")
538	            else
539	              @on_skip.call(key, "not a regular file")
540	            end
541	          end
542	        end
543	        found.sort_by(&:key)
544	      end
545	
546	      # The directory's path with symlinks resolved (the directory itself
547	      # may be one). Raises Error if it is missing or not a directory.
548	      def real_root
549	        @real_root ||= begin
550	          raise Error, "#{@root}: no such directory" unless File.exist?(@root)
551	          raise Error, "#{@root}: not a directory" unless File.directory?(@root)
552	
553	          File.realpath(@root).b
554	        rescue SystemCallError => e
555	          raise Error, "cannot read directory #{@root}: #{self.class.reason(e)}"
556	        end
557	      end
558	
559	      # The Target for writing key's file, or nil (reported via on_skip) if
560	      # key isn't a valid key, or writing there would mean following or
561	      # replacing a symlink or replacing a special file: as when walking,
562	      # symlinks are never followed, so nothing is written outside the
563	      # directory. Raises PathConflict if a file is in the way of one of the
564	      # key's directories, or a directory is where its file would go. Only
565	      # looks: nothing is created.
566	      def target(key)
567	        unless self.class.valid_key?(key)
568	          # The key came from elsewhere and may not even be printable.
569	          @on_skip.call(key.inspect, "not a valid key")
570	          return nil
571	        end
572	
573	        segments = key.split("/")
574	        path = real_root
575	        segments.each_with_index do |segment, i|
576	          path = File.join(path, segment.b)
577	          rel = segments[0..i].join("/")
578	          stat = lstat(path, rel)
579	          last = i == segments.size - 1
580	          if stat.nil?
581	            # Nothing there: the rest of the path is created when writing.
582	            return Target.new(key: key, path: File.join(real_root, key.b), stat: nil)
583	          elsif stat.symlink?
584	            @on_skip.call(key, last ? "symbolic link" : "#{rel} is a symbolic link")
585	            return nil
586	          elsif !last && !stat.directory?
587	            raise PathConflict.new(key, "#{rel} is not a directory")
588	          elsif last && stat.directory?
589	            raise PathConflict.new(key, "it is a directory")
590	          elsif last && !stat.file?
591	            @on_skip.call(key, "not a regular file")
592	            return nil
593	          elsif last
594	            return Target.new(key: key, path: path, stat: stat)
595	          end
596	        end
597	      end
598	
599	      # Replaces target's file with what the block writes to the IO it is
600	      # given. The contents are staged in a file next to it and renamed over
601	      # it only once complete, so the file is never seen half-written and is
602	      # left as it was if the block raises. Missing parent directories are
603	      # created; a replaced file keeps its permissions.
604	      def write(target)
605	        dir = File.dirname(target.path)
606	        make_parent_dirs(target.key)
607	        staged = File.join(dir, "#{STAGING_PREFIX}#{SecureRandom.hex(8)}#{STAGING_SUFFIX}")
608	        File.open(staged, File::WRONLY | File::CREAT | File::EXCL | File::NOFOLLOW | File::BINARY, 0o666) do |file|
609	          yield file
610	          file.chmod(target.stat.mode & 0o7777) if target.stat
611	          file.fsync
612	        end
613	        # A symlink swapped into the path meanwhile must not carry the file
614	        # outside the directory.
615	        unless File.realpath(dir).b == File.dirname(File.join(real_root, target.key.b))
616	          raise Error, "cannot write #{target.key}: its directory has moved"
617	        end
618	
619	        File.rename(staged, target.path)
620	        staged = nil
621	      rescue SystemCallError, IOError => e
622	        raise Error, "cannot write #{target.key}: #{self.class.reason(e)}"
623	      ensure
624	        begin
625	          File.unlink(staged) if staged
626	        rescue SystemCallError
627	          nil # never created, or already gone
628	        end
629	      end
630	
631	      private
632	
633	      def make_parent_dirs(key)
634	        path = real_root
635	        key.split("/")[0...-1].each do |segment|
636	          path = File.join(path, segment.b)
637	          begin
638	            Dir.mkdir(path)
639	          rescue Errno::EEXIST
640	            nil # checked by target; anything else fails when writing
641	          end
642	        end
643	      end
644	
645	      def children(dir, rel)
646	        Dir.children(dir, encoding: Encoding::BINARY)
647	      rescue SystemCallError => e
648	        raise Error, "cannot read directory #{rel ? display(rel) : @root}: #{self.class.reason(e)}"
649	      end
650	
651	      def lstat(path, rel)
652	        File.lstat(path)
653	      rescue Errno::ENOENT
654	        nil # removed while walking
655	      rescue SystemCallError => e
656	        raise Error, "cannot read #{display(rel)}: #{self.class.reason(e)}"
657	      end
658	
659	      def display(rel)
660	        rel.dup.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8).scrub
661	      end
662	    end
663	  end
664	end

674	    # A parsed command line: syncbox <command> <dir> --server <url>.

676	    Options = Data.define(:command, :dir, :server) do

680	
681	      # Returns Options, or nil if help was requested.
682	      def self.parse(argv, env = ENV)
683	        server = nil
684	        help = false
685	        parser = OptionParser.new do |o|
686	          o.banner = usage
687	          o.on("--server URL", String, "Syncbox server base URL (env: SYNCBOX_SERVER, required)") { |v| server = v }
688	          o.on("-h", "--help") { help = true }
689	        end

691	        return nil if help
692	
693	        raise UsageError, "missing command" if command.nil?
694	        raise UsageError, "unknown command: #{command}" unless COMMANDS.include?(command)
695	        raise UsageError, "missing <dir>" if dir.nil? || dir.empty?
696	        raise UsageError, "unexpected argument: #{rest.first}" unless rest.empty?

709	          raise UsageError, "--server must be an http:// or https:// URL, got #{raw.inspect}"
710	        end

715	      end

723	  module Client
724	    # syncbox pull: downloads every blob that is missing locally or whose
725	    # local copy has different contents (by SHA-256), to the file named by
726	    # its key inside the directory. Files identical to the server's version
727	    # are not downloaded again; local files the server doesn't have are left
728	    # alone.
729	    class Pull
730	      Result = Data.define(:downloaded, :unchanged)
731	
732	      def initialize(local_dir, remote, out: $stdout)
733	        @local_dir = local_dir
734	        @remote = remote
735	        @out = out
736	      end
737	
738	      def run
739	        @local_dir.real_root # fail before contacting the server
740	        downloaded = 0
741	        unchanged = 0
742	        @remote.list.each do |blob|
743	          target = @local_dir.target(blob["key"])
744	          next unless target
745	
746	          if target.stat && same?(target, blob)
747	            unchanged += 1
748	            next
749	          end
750	
751	          @local_dir.write(target) do |file|
752	            @remote.get(target.key) { |chunk| file.write(chunk) }
753	          end
754	          downloaded += 1
755	          @out.puts "downloaded #{target.key}"
756	        end
757	
758	        Result.new(downloaded: downloaded, unchanged: unchanged).tap do |result|
759	          @out.puts "pull: #{result.downloaded} downloaded, #{result.unchanged} unchanged"
760	        end
761	      end
762	
763	      private
764	
765	      # Files of different sizes differ; only equal sizes need hashing.
766	      def same?(target, blob)
767	        return false if blob["size"].is_a?(Integer) && blob["size"] != target.stat.size
768	
769	        LocalDir.sha256(target) == blob["sha256"]
770	      end
771	    end
772	  end

778	    # syncbox push: uploads every local file that the server lacks or holds
779	    # with different contents (by SHA-256). Files identical to the server's
780	    # version are not sent again; blobs that exist only on the server are
781	    # left alone.
782	    class Push
783	      Result = Data.define(:uploaded, :unchanged)
784	
785	      def initialize(local_dir, remote, out: $stdout)
786	        @local_dir = local_dir
787	        @remote = remote
788	        @out = out
789	      end

792	        entries = @local_dir.entries
793	        remote_sha256 = @remote.list.to_h { |blob| [blob["key"], blob["sha256"]] }
794	
795	        uploaded = 0
796	        entries.each do |entry|
797	          next if remote_sha256[entry.key] == LocalDir.sha256(entry)
798	
799	          upload(entry)
800	          uploaded += 1
801	          @out.puts "uploaded #{entry.key}"
802	        end
803	
804	        Result.new(uploaded: uploaded, unchanged: entries.size - uploaded).tap do |result|
805	          @out.puts "push: #{result.uploaded} uploaded, #{result.unchanged} unchanged"
806	        end
807	      end

811	      def upload(entry)
812	        file = begin
813	          File.open(entry.path, File::RDONLY | File::NOFOLLOW | File::BINARY)
814	        rescue SystemCallError => e
815	          raise Error, "cannot read #{entry.key}: #{LocalDir.reason(e)}"
816	        end
817	        begin
818	          @remote.put(entry.key, file, file.size)
819	        ensure
820	          file.close
821	        end
822	      end
823	    end

828	require "json"
829	require "net/http"
830	require "openssl"
831	require "uri"
832	
833	module Syncbox
834	  module Client
835	    # The Syncbox HTTP API (syncbox-openapi.yaml) over one keep-alive
836	    # connection. Network failures and unexpected answers raise Error.
837	    class Remote
838	      OPEN_TIMEOUT = 10
839	      READ_TIMEOUT = 60
840	      WRITE_TIMEOUT = 60
841	
842	      # Failures of the connection itself, as opposed to an HTTP answer.
843	      NETWORK_ERRORS = [
844	        SystemCallError, SocketError, IOError, EOFError, Timeout::Error,
845	        OpenSSL::SSL::SSLError, Net::HTTPBadResponse, Net::ProtocolError
846	      ].freeze
847	
848	      # Carries an error raised by a caller's block out through Net::HTTP, so
849	      # that a local failure (say, a full disk) isn't reported as a network one.
850	      class BlockError < StandardError
851	        attr_reader :error
852	
853	        def initialize(error)
854	          super(error.message)
855	          @error = error
856	        end
857	      end
858	      private_constant :BlockError
859	
860	      # Yields a Remote for base_url (a URI::HTTP) and closes its connection.
861	      def self.open(base_url)
862	        remote = new(base_url)
863	        yield remote
864	      ensure
865	        remote&.close
866	      end
867	
868	      def initialize(base_url)
869	        @base_url = base_url
870	        @base_path = base_url.path.chomp("/")
871	        @http = Net::HTTP.new(base_url.host, base_url.port)
872	        @http.use_ssl = base_url.scheme == "https"
873	        @http.open_timeout = OPEN_TIMEOUT
874	        @http.read_timeout = READ_TIMEOUT
875	        @http.write_timeout = WRITE_TIMEOUT
876	        # A body cut short of its Content-Length is an error, not the whole blob.
877	        @http.ignore_eof = false
878	        # PUT is idempotent, but a retried streamed body would be sent empty.
879	        @http.max_retries = 0
880	      end
881	
882	      def close
883	        @http.finish if @http.started?
884	      end
885	
886	      # GET /blobs: [{"key", "size", "sha256", "modified_at"}].
887	      def list
888	        response = request(Net::HTTP::Get.new("#{@base_path}/blobs"))
889	        expect(response, "200", "GET /blobs")
890	        entries = JSON.parse(response.body)
891	        unless entries.is_a?(Array) && entries.all? { |e| e.is_a?(Hash) && e["key"].is_a?(String) && e["sha256"].is_a?(String) }
892	          raise Error, "unexpected response from server to GET /blobs: not a list of blobs"
893	        end
894	
895	        entries
896	      rescue JSON::ParserError
897	        raise Error, "unexpected response from server to GET /blobs: invalid JSON"
898	      end
899	
900	      # GET /blobs/{key}, yielding the body in chunks as they arrive. Errors
901	      # raised by the block propagate unchanged.
902	      def get(key)
903	        # identity: the body is the blob's bytes as stored, nothing to decode.
904	        req = Net::HTTP::Get.new(blob_path(key), "accept-encoding" => "identity")
905	        request(req) do |response|
906	          expect(response, "200", "GET #{key}")
907	          response.read_body do |chunk|
908	            yield chunk
909	          rescue StandardError => e
910	            raise BlockError, e
911	          end
912	        end
913	      rescue BlockError => e
914	        raise e.error
915	      end
916	
917	      # PUT /blobs/{key}, streaming size bytes from io as the body.
918	      def put(key, io, size)
919	        req = Net::HTTP::Put.new(blob_path(key))
920	        req["content-type"] = "application/octet-stream"
921	        req.content_length = size
922	        req.body_stream = io
923	        expect(request(req), "201", "PUT #{key}")
924	      end
925	
926	      # Percent-encodes each segment of a key; "/" stays a separator.
927	      def self.escape_key(key)
928	        key.split("/", -1).map { |segment| URI.encode_uri_component(segment) }.join("/")
929	      end
930	
931	      private
932	
933	      def blob_path(key)
934	        "#{@base_path}/blobs/#{self.class.escape_key(key)}"
935	      end
936	
937	      # With a block, the response body is left for the block to read; if the
938	      # block raises, Net::HTTP drops the connection.
939	      def request(req, &block)
940	        @http.start unless @http.started?
941	        @http.request(req, &block)
942	      rescue *NETWORK_ERRORS => e
943	        @http.finish if @http.started?
944	        raise Error, "cannot reach server #{@base_url}: #{network_reason(e)}"
945	      end
946	
947	      def network_reason(error)
948	        case error
949	        when Timeout::Error then "timed out"
950	        when SystemCallError then LocalDir.reason(error)
951	        else error.message
952	        end
953	      end
954	
955	      def expect(response, code, what)
956	        return response if response.code == code
957	
958	        detail = response.body.to_s.lines.first.to_s.strip[0, 200]
959	        raise Error, "server answered #{what} with HTTP #{response.code}#{": #{detail}" unless detail.empty?}"
960	      end
961	    end
962	  end
963	end

966	module Syncbox
967	  module Client
968	    # syncbox status: a dry run of push and pull. Compares the directory with
969	    # GET /blobs by key and SHA-256 and prints what push would upload and
970	    # what pull would download, by the same rules (a file whose contents
971	    # differ is listed both ways). Changes nothing on either side: the only
972	    # request is GET /blobs, and local files are only read.
973	    #
974	    #   upload    new      <key>   only here, the server lacks it
975	    #   upload    changed  <key>   the server's blob has other contents
976	    #   download  changed  <key>   the local file has other contents
977	    #   download  new      <key>   only on the server
978	    #   status: 2 to upload, 2 to download, 1 unchanged
979	    class Status
980	      Change = Data.define(:direction, :kind, :key)
981	      Result = Data.define(:uploads, :downloads, :unchanged)
982	
983	      def initialize(local_dir, remote, out: $stdout, err: $stderr)
984	        @local_dir = local_dir
985	        @remote = remote
986	        @out = out
987	        @err = err
988	      end
989	
990	      def run
991	        local_sha256 = @local_dir.entries.to_h { |entry| [entry.key, LocalDir.sha256(entry)] }
992	        blobs = @remote.list.sort_by { |blob| blob["key"] }
993	        remote_sha256 = blobs.to_h { |blob| [blob["key"], blob["sha256"]] }
994	
995	        # As push: every local file the server lacks or holds with other contents.
996	        uploads = local_sha256.filter_map do |key, sha256|
997	          next if remote_sha256[key] == sha256
998	
999	          Change.new(direction: "upload", kind: remote_sha256.key?(key) ? "changed" : "new", key: key)
1000	        end
1001	
1002	        # As pull: every blob whose file is missing or has other contents,
1003	        # skipping the keys pull would skip.
1004	        unchanged = 0
1005	        downloads = blobs.filter_map do |blob|
1006	          target = download_target(blob["key"])
1007	          next unless target
1008	
1009	          if target.stat.nil?
1010	            Change.new(direction: "download", kind: "new", key: target.key)
1011	          elsif local_sha256.fetch(target.key) { LocalDir.sha256(target) } == blob["sha256"]
1012	            unchanged += 1
1013	            nil
1014	          else
1015	            Change.new(direction: "download", kind: "changed", key: target.key)
1016	          end
1017	        end
1018	
1019	        Result.new(uploads: uploads, downloads: downloads, unchanged: unchanged).tap { |result| report(result) }
1020	      end
1021	
1022	      private
1023	
1024	      # Where pull would write key, or nil if it would skip it (reported via
1025	      # the directory's on_skip) or fail to write it (reported here).
1026	      def download_target(key)
1027	        @local_dir.target(key)
1028	      rescue LocalDir::PathConflict => e
1029	        @err.puts "syncbox: cannot download #{e.key}: #{e.reason}"
1030	        nil
1031	      end
1032	
1033	      def report(result)
1034	        (result.uploads + result.downloads).each do |change|
1035	          @out.puts format("%-9s %-8s %s", change.direction, change.kind, change.key)
1036	        end
1037	        if result.uploads.empty? && result.downloads.empty?
1038	          @out.puts "status: in sync, #{result.unchanged} unchanged"
1039	        else
1040	          @out.puts "status: #{result.uploads.size} to upload, #{result.downloads.size} to download, " \
1041	                    "#{result.unchanged} unchanged"
1042	        end
1043	      end
1044	    end
1045	  end
1046	end

# Syncbox (Ruby)

Self-hosted file storage with sync: HTTP server + CLI client.
Contract: [SYNCBOX-SPEC.md](SYNCBOX-SPEC.md), [syncbox-openapi.yaml](syncbox-openapi.yaml).

Everything runs in Docker via `docker compose` (Ruby 3.3.12, `ruby:3.3.12` image);
nothing needs to be installed on the host besides Docker.

## Server

```sh
./run-server --data-dir <path> [--port <n>]   # port defaults to 8080
SYNCBOX_DATA_DIR=<path> SYNCBOX_PORT=<n> ./run-server
```

Flags take precedence over environment variables. The data dir is created if
missing and bind-mounted into the container; the port is published on
`127.0.0.1` (override with `SYNCBOX_PUBLISH_ADDR=0.0.0.0`). The server runs in
the foreground; SIGTERM/SIGINT stop it gracefully and remove the container.

Implemented endpoints: `GET /healthz`, `GET /blobs`, `PUT /blobs/{key}`, `GET /blobs/{key}`,
`DELETE /blobs/{key}`. Blobs are stored under `<data-dir>/blobs/<key>`; uploads
are staged in `<data-dir>/tmp`.

### Atomic uploads

`PUT` streams the body into a fresh staging file `<data-dir>/tmp/<random>.part`
(fsynced), then `rename(2)`s it over `<data-dir>/blobs/<key>`. Consequences:

- A `GET` or `GET /blobs` sees either the whole old blob or the whole new one,
  never a partial write; a download already in progress keeps streaming the
  version it opened.
- Concurrent `PUT`s to the same key each report the hash of their own body; the
  last rename wins and the stored blob is one of the uploaded bodies, intact.
  `PUT`s to different keys share nothing but the directories above them.
- Parent directories of a new key are created only after the whole body is staged.
- Staging files are outside `blobs/`, so they're never listed or reachable by
  any key, and they are removed when the request ends, whether it succeeded or
  failed. A body cut short by the client never reaches the app (Puma buffers
  the body first). Files left by a server killed mid-upload are removed on the
  next start.
- On startup the server checks that a file can be renamed from `tmp/` into
  `blobs/`, and refuses to start if not (e.g. `blobs/` is a separate
  filesystem or mount): `rename(2)` is atomic only within one mount and fails
  with `EXDEV` across mounts — it never falls back to copying.

Coordination between several server processes on one data dir is out of scope.

`GET /blobs` returns `[{"key", "size", "sha256", "modified_at"}]` for every
regular file under `<data-dir>/blobs`, sorted by key (`modified_at` is the file
mtime, ISO 8601 UTC). Files placed there directly are listed too; symlinks,
special files and names that aren't valid UTF-8 are skipped. Hashes are
computed on each request.

`DELETE /blobs/{key}` answers `204` (no body) when the blob was removed and `404`
when there is none — directories and symlinks are not blobs, so they are never
followed or removed. Directories left empty by a delete are pruned, so their
paths can become keys again.

### Keys and directory traversal

A key is a relative POSIX path (`docs/readme.txt`). `PUT`, `GET` and `DELETE
/blobs/{key}` answer `400` for a key that:

- contains a `..` segment, or a `.`/empty segment (`a//b`, `a/`), or is absolute
  (`/etc/passwd`, `%2Fetc%2Fpasswd`) — `%2F` counts as a separator, `%2e` as a dot;
- can't be a file name here: not valid UTF-8 after percent-decoding (incl.
  encoded surrogates and overlong forms such as `%C0%AE`), contains NUL, has
  malformed percent-escapes, or exceeds `NAME_MAX`/`PATH_MAX`.

`..` inside a name (`a..b`, `...`) is an ordinary character sequence. On top
of these textual checks the store confines the actual disk path: the
normalized path must lie strictly inside `<data-dir>/blobs`, and resolving it
with `realpath` must not change it, so a symlink placed in the store by hand is
never followed (`PUT` through it is `400`, `GET`/`DELETE` are `404`). The data
dir itself may be a symlink.

## Client

```sh
./run-client push <dir> --server <url>
./run-client pull <dir> --server <url>
./run-client status <dir> --server <url>
SYNCBOX_SERVER=<url> ./run-client push <dir>
```

`--server` takes precedence over `SYNCBOX_SERVER`; it must be an `http://` or
`https://` URL (a path prefix such as `http://host/syncbox` is allowed). The
client runs in the `client` compose service: `<dir>` must be an existing
directory and is bind-mounted into the container (read-only for `status`),
which uses the host's network, so `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` reaches a server
started with `run-server` on this machine. SIGTERM/SIGINT stop the container.

`push` walks `<dir>` recursively, hashes every regular file with SHA-256 and
compares it with `GET /blobs`. It `PUT`s the files that the server lacks or holds
with a different hash, under the file's relative POSIX path as the key
(`docs/readme.txt`). Files identical to the server's version are not sent again,
and blobs that exist only on the server are left alone. Each upload is printed
(`uploaded <key>`), then a summary (`push: N uploaded, M unchanged`).
Symlinks (never followed), special files and names that aren't valid UTF-8
are skipped with a warning on stderr.

`pull` is the reverse: it fetches `GET /blobs`, and `GET`s every blob that is
missing in `<dir>` or whose local file has a different SHA-256, writing it to
the key's relative POSIX path and creating directories as needed. Files
identical to the server's version are not downloaded again, and local files
the server doesn't have are left alone. Each download is printed
(`downloaded <key>`), then a summary (`pull: N downloaded, M unchanged`).
A download is streamed into a staging file next to its target
(`.syncbox-<random>.part`, removed on failure) and renamed over it once
complete, so a failed or interrupted pull never leaves a half-written file; a
body cut short of its `Content-Length` counts as a failure. A replaced file
keeps its permissions. Keys come from the server, so pull never writes
outside `<dir>`: keys that aren't plain relative paths (`..`, absolute, empty
or `.` segments, NUL) are skipped with a warning, and so are keys whose path
runs through a symlink (never followed) or ends at a symlink or special file
(never replaced).

`status` is a dry run of `push` and `pull`: it compares `<dir>` with
`GET /blobs` by key and SHA-256, by the same rules, and prints what they would
do, changing nothing on either side. Its only request is `GET /blobs` (no
`PUT`/`DELETE`, not even a blob download), local files are only read, and
`run-client` mounts `<dir>` read-only for it. Each difference is one line,
uploads first, then downloads, each sorted by key:

```
upload    new      local-only.txt      # push would upload it; the server lacks it
upload    changed  both.txt            # push would upload it; the server's copy differs
download  changed  both.txt            # pull would download it; the local copy differs
download  new      docs/remote.txt     # pull would download it; it is missing locally
status: 2 to upload, 2 to download, 1 unchanged
```

A file whose contents differ is listed in both directions, as `push` and `pull`
would each overwrite the other side's copy; which one wins is up to `sync`.
With no differences it prints `status: in sync, N unchanged`. It skips, with the
same warnings, whatever `push` and `pull` would skip; a key that `pull` couldn't
write because a file or directory is in the way is reported on stderr
(`syncbox: cannot download a/b: a is not a directory`) instead of failing.
Exit status is `0` whenever the comparison succeeds, whether or not anything
differs.

Exit status: `0` on success, `2` for a bad command line, `1` if the command
fails (server unreachable, the server rejects a request, a local file can't be
read or written, a file is in the way of a directory or the other way round
during a pull): the client prints the reason to stderr and stops at the first
failure.

`sync` accepts the same arguments but is not implemented yet: it prints a
message saying so and exits with `1`.

## Tests

```sh
./run-tests
```

Runs the Minitest suite (`test/`) inside the `tests` compose service.

## Layout

- `bin/syncbox-server` — server entry point (inside the container)
- `bin/syncbox` — client CLI entry point (inside the container)
- `lib/syncbox/server/config.rb` — flag/env configuration
- `lib/syncbox/server/app.rb` — Rack app (HTTP API)
- `lib/syncbox/server/store.rb` — blob storage on disk, key validation
- `lib/syncbox/server/runner.rb` — Puma boot
- `lib/syncbox/client/cli.rb`, `options.rb` — client command line
- `lib/syncbox/client/local_dir.rb` — walking, hashing and safely writing the local directory
- `lib/syncbox/client/remote.rb` — HTTP API client
- `lib/syncbox/client/push.rb`, `pull.rb`, `status.rb` — `push`, `pull`, `status`
- `compose.yaml`, `Dockerfile` — container setup; `run-server`, `run-client`, `run-tests` — wrappers
FROM ruby:3.3.12

WORKDIR /app

ENV BUNDLE_FROZEN=true

COPY Gemfile Gemfile.lock ./
RUN bundle install --jobs 4 --retry 3

COPY . .
name: syncbox

x-app: &app
  build: .
  image: syncbox-ruby:dev
  init: true
  # Run as the host user so files in bind-mounted directories stay owned by them.
  user: "${SYNCBOX_UID:-1000}:${SYNCBOX_GID:-1000}"
  environment:
    HOME: /tmp

services:
  server:
    <<: *app
    command: ["bin/syncbox-server", "--data-dir", "/data", "--port", "${SYNCBOX_PORT:-8080}"]
    ports:
      - "${SYNCBOX_PUBLISH_ADDR:-127.0.0.1}:${SYNCBOX_PORT:-8080}:${SYNCBOX_PORT:-8080}"
    volumes:
      - type: bind
        source: "${SYNCBOX_HOST_DATA_DIR:-./data}"
        target: /data

  # `run client <command> /sync --server <url>`; run-client mounts the local
  # directory at /sync. Host networking, so that the server URL means the same
  # inside the container as on the host (e.g. a server on 127.0.0.1:<port>).
  client:
    <<: *app
    entrypoint: ["bin/syncbox"]
    network_mode: host
    volumes:
      - type: bind
        source: "${SYNCBOX_HOST_SYNC_DIR:-./sync}"
        target: /sync
        # run-client sets this for status, which must not change the directory.
        read_only: ${SYNCBOX_SYNC_READ_ONLY:-false}

  tests:
    <<: *app
    command: ["bundle", "exec", "rake", "test"]
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs the Syncbox client inside Docker (via docker compose).
#
#   run-client <push|pull|sync|status> <dir> --server <url>
#
# --server falls back to SYNCBOX_SERVER. <dir> is bind-mounted into the
# container; the container uses the host's network, so the server URL means
# the same as it does here (read-only for status). Exits with the client's
# status.
set -euo pipefail

root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

usage() {
  echo "Usage: run-client <push|pull|sync|status> <dir> --server <url>" >&2
  exit 2
}

die() {
  echo "run-client: $*" >&2
  usage
}

server="${SYNCBOX_SERVER:-}"
positional=()

while (($#)); do
  case "$1" in
    --server) (($# >= 2)) || die "--server requires a value"; server="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --server=*) server="${1#*=}"; shift ;;
    -h | --help) usage ;;
    --) shift; positional+=("$@"); break ;;
    -*) die "unknown option: $1" ;;
    *) positional+=("$1"); shift ;;
  esac
done

((${#positional[@]} >= 1)) || die "missing command"
command="${positional[0]}"
case "$command" in
  push | pull | sync | status) ;;
  *) die "unknown command: $command" ;;
esac
((${#positional[@]} >= 2)) || die "missing <dir>"
((${#positional[@]} == 2)) || die "unexpected argument: ${positional[2]}"
dir="${positional[1]}"
[[ -n "$dir" ]] || die "missing <dir>"
[[ -n "$server" ]] || die "--server (or SYNCBOX_SERVER) is required"

if [[ ! -e "$dir" ]]; then
  echo "run-client: $dir: no such directory" >&2
  exit 1
elif [[ ! -d "$dir" ]]; then
  echo "run-client: $dir: not a directory" >&2
  exit 1
fi

export SYNCBOX_HOST_SYNC_DIR="$(cd -- "$dir" && pwd -P)"
export SYNCBOX_UID="$(id -u)" SYNCBOX_GID="$(id -g)"
# status is a dry run: give it the directory read-only.
if [[ "$command" == status ]]; then
  export SYNCBOX_SYNC_READ_ONLY=true
else
  export SYNCBOX_SYNC_READ_ONLY=false
fi

compose=(docker compose --project-directory "$root" -f "$root/compose.yaml")

# `docker compose run` does not forward SIGTERM to the container and leaves it
# running when killed, so stop our container explicitly on shutdown signals.
container="syncbox-client-$$"
child=""
stopping=""

stop_container() {
  # Retry briefly in case the signal arrived before the container was created.
  for _ in $(seq 50); do
    docker stop --time 10 "$container" >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
    kill -0 "$child" 2>/dev/null || return 0
    sleep 0.2
  done
}

on_signal() {
  trap '' TERM INT HUP
  stopping=1
  if [[ -n "$child" ]]; then stop_container; fi
  return 0
}

trap on_signal TERM INT HUP

"${compose[@]}" build --quiet client >&2
[[ -z "$stopping" ]] || exit 130

# -T: no pseudo-TTY, so the client's stdout and stderr stay separate streams.
"${compose[@]}" run --rm -T --name "$container" client "$command" /sync --server "$server" &
child=$!
if [[ -n "$stopping" ]]; then stop_container; fi

while kill -0 "$child" 2>/dev/null; do
  wait "$child" || true
done
status=0
wait "$child" || status=$?
[[ -z "$stopping" ]] || exit 130
exit "$status"

module Syncbox
  module Client
    # Entry point of the syncbox executable; returns the exit status.
    module CLI
      IMPLEMENTED = %w[push pull status].freeze

      def self.run(argv, env: ENV, out: $stdout, err: $stderr)
        options = Options.parse(argv, env)
        if options.nil?
          out.puts Options.usage
          return 0
        end

        unless IMPLEMENTED.include?(options.command)
          err.puts "syncbox: '#{options.command}' is not implemented yet (available: #{IMPLEMENTED.join(', ')})"
          return 1
        end

        local_dir = LocalDir.new(options.dir, on_skip: ->(path, why) { err.puts "syncbox: skipping #{path}: #{why}" })
        Remote.open(options.server) do |remote|
          case options.command
          when "push" then Push.new(local_dir, remote, out: out).run
          when "pull" then Pull.new(local_dir, remote, out: out).run
          when "status" then Status.new(local_dir, remote, out: out, err: err).run
          end
        end
        0
      rescue UsageError => e
        err.puts "syncbox: #{e.message}", Options.usage
        2
      rescue Error => e
        err.puts "syncbox: #{e.message}"
        1
      end
    end
  end
end
